exposure: Antibiotic therapy in the neonatal period
cohort: The study included 100 mother-child pairs where all children were born from uncomplicated and term pregnancies (between 37 and 42 weeks of gestation).
finding: Perinatal factors related to intestinal permeability are important during the first 3 months of infant life, with antibiotic therapy showing a negative but reversible influence on intestinal integrity, and probiotic therapy positively reducing endotoxemia.
mod_finding: The mode of delivery had no significant influence on the parameters of infant intestinal leakage (fecal zonulin, occludin, LPS concentrations) during the first year of life.
